details:
Since VRchat avatars typically follow a similar bone layout, a lot of animations will typically work across most avatars. That said, normally these animations are specific to an individual avatar that they are attached to.

What I'd like to suggest is allowing players to create a custom library of animations that they can register or upload that they can then play from an extra expressions menu on any avatar. A simple example of this might be a basic sit animation, which a lot of avatars lack, but other options such as dances, gestures, etc. would all be possible.

Avatars with more unique bone layouts or missing bones might get a bit wonky when playing animations not custom made for them, but as most avatars follow a similar structure, this would still allow adding additional animations to an avatar without needing to reupload it. This would also add a lot of expressiveness for both headset users and especially desktop users.

At base, the upload process would just need a way of specifying if an animation is play once or looped. In game, you'd just need a way to select which uploaded animations you wish to 'slot in' to your menu. Ideally the upload process wouldn't need to be as involved as it is for an avatar, since it's just an animation, and potentially might not require Unity at all since it hypothetically could be just a single file.
title: Universal In-Game Animation Library
